claims.statement: The scheduler is a one-node StateGraph (START -> launch -> END) registered as the `scheduler` graph, and its launch node deterministically routes a tick without invoking an LLM.

The scheduler routes task values for reconciliation, baby-sit, background-task monitoring, workspace refresh including the legacy refresh name, session/agent cost, feedback, and human-review deadlines; unrecognized tasks fall through to scheduled-automation launch.
Scheduler branches return missing-key statuses for absent watch, thread, review, or schedule routing data, and convert exhausted transient sandbox attachment errors to `sandbox_unavailable`.
Stored agent schedules normalize and validate five-field cron expressions, including range-checked values, lists, ranges, and steps.
Scheduled automation launch resolves the stored schedule and fired trigger, cleans up orphaned or mismatched triggers, and launches a fresh agent schedule only for a valid schedule trigger.
`reconcile_stale_runs` paginates busy threads, lists pending runs, and interrupts those older than its default 1,800-second age threshold to free threads whose completion webhook was lost.
The stale-run sweep skips invalid timestamps, isolates failures per thread, ends safely on thread-search failure, and returns checked, stale, and cancelled counts.

Session-cost refresh is a bounded chain of self-deleting delayed scheduler runs using delays of 15, 30, 60, 120, and 240 seconds; a pending refresh schedules the next attempt while unavailable or exhausted results clear the Slack pending marker and terminate.

A baby-sit watch is persisted in `baby_sit_watches` under a lower-cased owner/repo and PR-number key and binds the originating thread, head SHA/ref, installation, run configuration, source context, retry/deduplication data, and cron ID.
Only one active agent thread may own a PR watch; restarting on the same head carries retry and deduplication state, while a changed head starts that state over.
Baby-sit start ensures a UTC `*/10 * * * *` scheduler cron, reuses one matching tagged cron while deleting duplicates, and rolls back a brand-new store row and partial cron when cron creation fails.

Signed GitHub webhooks are verified at the route boundary, and completed CI payload handling matches active watches by repository plus SHA or branch, updates an installation ID, and deduplicates delivery IDs before evaluation.
Cron and webhook baby-sit triggers share a five-minute per-watch lock implemented with a short-lived lock thread, so concurrent evaluation returns `busy` rather than dispatching twice.

A baby-sit head change resets retry and failure/alert deduplication state; a new failing state dispatches an untrusted-signal-aware continuation to the originating thread and is deduplicated by a head-SHA and retry-count fingerprint.
Flaky reruns are capped at three per head SHA; retry recording verifies active watch ownership and SHA, increments durable retry state, and posts an alert only once for a head/check/safe-URL key.

A green watch dispatches a ready run then stops, while blocked checks, retry exhaustion, and repeated evaluation errors finish the watch by attempting source notification and falling back to an enqueued terminal baby-sit run on the originating thread.

The `manage_baby_sit` tool is the agent-facing interface for start, stop, and retry recording; it requires canonical PR URLs and an executable thread, verifies open-PR and GitHub-App prerequisites for start, and enforces watch ownership for stop and retries.

Background-task monitoring uses either a callback or an idempotent per-thread every-minute scheduler cron, atomically claims terminal tasks before enqueuing their completion to the owning thread, and deletes monitor crons only after a locked recheck finds no running or undelivered terminal task.

`schedule_thread_wakeup` creates a thread-bound one-shot cron directly against the `agent` assistant for delays from one minute through 24 hours, rounds its fire time to a minute, and sets an end time 90 seconds later.

Wakeups are limited to 10 between human messages using a generation derived from the latest human input and persisted count in thread metadata; system messages do not reset the generation and the count is recorded before cron creation.

Because wakeup cron rows remain after firing, scheduling best-effort purges only expired crons tagged `thread_wakeup`, fully paging before deletion; explicit cancellation is scoped to that thread and cron kind.

Agent-cost refresh obtains run-only LangSmith cost and persists it to invocation analytics, retrying retrieval or persistence failure through the same fixed five-delay budget but terminating for invalid payload or explicitly unavailable LangSmith access.
Focused tests cover scheduler workspace dispatch, baby-sit lifecycle/concurrency/deduplication, and wakeup validation, configuration, rate limits, cancellation, and cleanup.

Feedback prompts are delivered through a self-deleting delayed `thread_feedback` scheduler run only after the stored feedback record still matches, the latest run is successful, and the thread has been quiet for five minutes; otherwise the handler skips or reschedules for the remaining delay.

Workspace refresh crons are staggered daily per workspace and scheduler-dispatched refreshes run full rebuilds from the base snapshot or update-only rebuilds from the current snapshot; failures retain the prior ready snapshot.

Workspace snapshots older than one hour can trigger a background update when no plausible refresh is in flight and the previous attempt is old enough; refresh runs are self-deleting scheduler runs and record their run ID on the workspace.
